steps.say: Stir sugar into water and it seems to disappear. The sugar has dissolved.
The sugar breaks into pieces too small to see. They spread out through the water.
The solid that dissolves is the solute. The liquid is the solvent, and the mixture is a solution.
Materials that dissolve are soluble, like salt. Materials that do not dissolve are insoluble, like sand.
Stirring, warmer water and smaller grains all make a solid dissolve faster.
Nothing is lost when a solid dissolves. 100 g of water and 10 g of salt make 110 g of solution.

check.prompt: Which of these is soluble in water?

options.why: Sand does not dissolve. It sinks to the bottom.
Chalk does not dissolve in water.
Pebbles do not dissolve in water.

hints: A soluble material dissolves and seems to disappear.
Think about what you stir into cooking water to add flavour.
Cross out the materials that sink to the bottom of a glass of water.
check.explanation: Salt dissolves in water, so it is soluble. Sand, chalk and pebbles are insoluble.

check.prompt: Ali dissolves 15 g of sugar in 150 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
hints: Dissolved sugar is still there, even when you cannot see it.
No mass is lost when a solid dissolves.
Add the mass of the sugar to the mass of the water.
check.explanation: 150 g + 15 g = 165 g. The sugar is still in the solution, so its mass is still there.
